challenges.name: The Leaky Hop
challenges.description:
The intruder tunnelled through an open proxy in the DMZ, so every session to PLC-01 wears the proxy's address. The SOC has filed attribution as impossible and moved on.

They gave up too early. Somewhere in edge_span_0200.pcapng the attacker's own machine spoke for itself - briefly, and more than once if you know where to look.

Recover the attacker's real IP and submit it; the correct address decrypts the flag.
hints: A proxy only relays what rides on the TCP stream it carries. Whatever the client had to arrange for itself never went through it.

challenges.name: The Impossible Levels
challenges.description:
All night the HMI swore tank T-101 sat calm and level. The field crew came back with a wet weir wall and a different opinion.

You have the plant's own records in tank_data.txt and the equipment sheet pump_curves.pdf. One of them is telling the truth; one of them is a story.

Work out how far the displayed level strayed from reality at its worst, and submit that peak deviation in metres, to two decimals. The right number decrypts the flag.
hints: A pump that is not running moves no water, whatever a column in the log may claim.

challenges.name: The Silent Safety System
challenges.description:
The level crossed High-High and the 2-out-of-3 safety vote should have slammed valve XV-101 shut. It did nothing - and it did it quietly, with no alarm and no reported mismatch.

safety_logic.bin is the compiled safety program that was running. Someone rewrote the vote so it could stay silent on command.

Find the override hidden inside and submit the bypass string it carries; it decrypts the flag.
hints: Three sensors vote, but the tamper lets two of them shout into a closed room - and a single word in the image decides when.

challenges.name: Ghost Rung
challenges.description:
The engineering workstation shows a clean ladder program. The controller is not running that program.

Everything you need is in the panel below. A rung lives in the PLC that the software will never draw for you - make it run, and read what it writes.

Submit the string it leaves in memory; it decrypts the flag.
hints: The workstation can only draw what the project claims exists. The gap between what is on disk and what is live is the whole challenge.

challenges.name: Cascade Complete
challenges.answer_placeholder: ASCII decoded from the 4-20 mA log
challenges.description:
Replay the intrusion end to end against a sandbox that runs the plant in real time. The attacker's own console is wired to it, and the credentials it demands are things you have already recovered.

Drive it the way they did, and watch what happens when the operators are handed a frozen, reassuring screen.

When the screen stops telling the truth, the plant itself is still talking. Recover the message it sends and submit it; it decrypts the flag.
hints: The console only trusts what you proved in earlier chapters; give it exactly those.
A lamp can be held on while the thing behind it flickers. Believe the measurement, not the indicator.

challenges.name: Hot Standby
challenges.answer_placeholder: revealed when the standby holds for 60 s
challenges.description:
The recovery key is in hand and restoration is under way when the primary PLC's watchdog faults - the implant's last move. The plant is about to fail over to a clean standby that carries no implant at all.

But the standby copies the primary's data blocks every few seconds, and recipe block %DB10 was poisoned hours ago. When failover lands, the clean controller will run the attacker's numbers faithfully.

Put %DB10 right on the primary before the next copy carries it across, complete the failover, and hold the plant steady. The panel will hand you a recovery token - submit it to decrypt the flag.
hints: A real number read in the wrong word order is still a real number - just a convincing lie. Trust the plant's engineering limits, not what the block shows.
